platform.ai.mcpServer.disableBody: Are you sure you want to turn off DataHub's MCP server? AI tools connected to it stop working until you turn it back on.

platform.ai.toolSelector.agentNote: An enabled agent runs with its own configured tools, regardless of this server's tool selection. It still acts as the calling user, so it cannot access data the user lacks permission to see.

platform.ai.mcpServers.baseInstructionsH: The base prompt this server serves. None uses only your custom instructions below. Small tells AI clients what DataHub is and when to use it; Large adds examples of which DataHub tool fits which job. Custom instructions are added after them.
platform.ai.mcpServers.instructionsPlace: Custom system prompt for this server's scope
platform.ai.mcpServers.toolsHelp: Select which tools this server exposes. When none are selected, all tools are available.
platform.ai.mcpServers.scopeHelp: Narrow down the assets this server's tools can search through on DataHub.
platform.ai.mcpServers.connectionUrlHelp: Point your MCP client at this URL.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.title: Connect a client
platform.ai.mcpConnect.subtitle: Add DataHub's MCP server to an AI tool.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.tokenAuthBody: DataHub token authentication is on, so every request needs a DataHub access token. Each request runs as the token's user, with that user's permissions. Replace <your-access-token> below with your token.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.noAuthBody: DataHub token authentication is off, so this URL accepts requests without a token. MCP calls run as DataHub's system user, with metadata writes on: to turn them off, edit the default server and switch off its Write Metadata tools. Keep this URL on a trusted network, and turn on token authentication before you share it.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.otherHint: Any client that supports Streamable HTTP
platform.ai.mcpConnect.claudeDesktopNote: This setup runs the mcp-remote bridge on your machine (it needs Node.js), so it works even when Anthropic's cloud can't reach DataHub. If DataHub has a public HTTPS URL, Claude (connector) needs nothing installed.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.connectorRecommen: The simplest way to use DataHub in Claude and Claude Desktop: nothing to install. Claude calls DataHub from Anthropic's cloud, so this URL must be reachable from the internet.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.connectorPrivateB: Claude calls custom connectors from Anthropic's cloud, so DataHub needs a public HTTPS URL, and this one looks private or isn't HTTPS. Use <local>Claude Desktop (local)</local> instead: it connects from your machine.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.connectorStepOpen: In Claude, open Customize → Connectors, select Add, then Add custom connector.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.connectorStepFiel: Enter a name and the remote MCP server URL, then click Continue.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.connectorStepHead: For Authentication, choose No sign-in. Open Request headers, choose {{header}}, and enter this value with your access token in place of the placeholder. Claude sends it exactly as entered, so keep the Bearer prefix.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.connectorTeamNote: On Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner adds the connector for everyone under Organization settings → Connectors.

On Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner adds the connector for everyone under Organization settings → Connectors, and its request header is shared: every member calls DataHub as the token's user. Use a token whose permissions suit everyone, or have each person connect with their own token through Claude Code or Claude Desktop (local).
platform.ai.mcpConnect.connectorHeadersB: Claude's Request headers are in beta and not every organization has them yet. If the dialog doesn't show them, use Claude Desktop (local) instead.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.chatGptTokenAuthT: ChatGPT can't connect to this DataHub yet
platform.ai.mcpConnect.chatGptTokenAuthB: DataHub token authentication is on, so every request needs a DataHub access token. ChatGPT can't send one: its custom MCP servers sign in only with OAuth or with no authentication, and DataHub's MCP server doesn't offer OAuth. Use <claude>Claude</claude>, <cursor>Cursor</cursor> or <claudeCode>Claude Code</claudeCode> instead, or another client from the tabs above.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.chatGptPrivateBod: ChatGPT calls custom MCP servers from OpenAI's servers, not from your computer, so DataHub needs a public HTTPS URL, and this one looks private or isn't HTTPS. Use <cursor>Cursor</cursor> or <claudeCode>Claude Code</claudeCode> instead: they connect from your machine. To reach a private server from ChatGPT, OpenAI offers <tunnel>Secure MCP Tunnel</tunnel>, which runs a tunnel client inside your network.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.chatGptPublicNoAu: Anyone who finds this URL can use DataHub

ChatGPT connects with no authentication, because DataHub token authentication is off. So can anyone else who finds this public URL, and every call runs as DataHub's system user, with metadata writes on unless you switch off the Write Metadata tools. Connect ChatGPT only to a DataHub whose metadata you are comfortable exposing. Turning token authentication on protects the URL, but ChatGPT can't connect then.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.chatGptStepOpen: In ChatGPT on the web, open Plugins, select the + button, then Add custom MCP server.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.chatGptStepFields: Enter a name, and under Connection, the Server URL.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.chatGptStepCreate: Review the risk warning, select I understand and want to continue, then Create as a plugin.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.chatGptStepUse: Install the plugin. In a conversation, type @ and select it.
platform.ai.mcpConnect.chatGptWorkspaceN: Your ChatGPT workspace's permissions decide whether you can add custom MCP servers. If you don't see the option, ask your workspace admin.
